Consult Summary:
25-year-old woman (Kim) with 2-day history of progressively worsening constant burning pain just inferior to the umbilicus, associated with mild nausea, subjective fever/sweats and pink-tinged urine; empirically treated today for presumed uncomplicated urinary tract infection and advised pregnancy testing and close follow-up.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Constant burning lower abdominal pain (below umbilicus).  
• Onset/duration: Began ~2 days ago, gradual onset, worsening.  
• Character: Burning, localized, non-radiating; worsens with palpation.  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Subjective fever/hot and sweaty (no measured temp).  
  – Mild nausea, no vomiting.  
  – Increased urinary frequency; urine noticed “pink” in color (possible hematuria).  
  – No dysuria, no urinary urgency, no flank pain.  
  – Constipation last week now resolved; currently normal bowel movements; no diarrhea.  
• Gynecologic/sexual: Sexually active with one partner, last intercourse 4 days ago. On etonogestrel implant (Implanon, inserted 1 year ago). Menses occurred ~2 weeks ago. No barrier contraception. Last STI screen 6 months ago (normal). No prior similar pain.  
• ROS screening negatives: No shortness of breath, cough, palpitations, headache, visual change.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: None specified.

Past Medical History:
• No chronic medical conditions reported.  
• No prior surgeries.

Medications:
• Etonogestrel implant (Implanon) – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• New prescription: Trimethoprim 300 mg? (tablet strength not specified) – 1 tablet twice daily for 3 days.  
• PRN recommendation: Paracetamol – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
Allergies: Not discussed (missing).

Social History:
• Lives in shared house with two roommates.  
• Occupation: Accountant.  
• Smoking: Denies.  
• Alcohol: Social use, “not more than normal.”  
• Recreational drugs: Not discussed.

Family History:
• Denies known relevant familial gastrointestinal or genitourinary disease.

Physical Examination:
• Vitals: Not recorded.  
• Abdominal exam: Not performed/recorded.  
• Other systems: Not recorded.

Investigations:
• None completed today.  
• Recommended:  
  – Urinalysis ± culture (not yet performed).  
  – Pregnancy test (patient advised to obtain).  
  – Additional tests discussed but not ordered pending response to empiric therapy.

Assessment & Plan:
Overall Impression:
Likely uncomplicated cystitis/UTI causing lower abdominal discomfort with possible hematuria; pregnancy and other intra-abdominal causes considered.

DDx Integration (brief):
1. Uncomplicated urinary tract infection/cystitis – supporting: pink urine, frequency, lower abdominal pain; opposing: absent dysuria.  
2. Early pregnancy/ectopic – supporting: lower abdominal pain, possible implant failure; opposing: contraception in place, last period 2 weeks ago.  
3. Gastrointestinal source (e.g., constipation, enteritis) – supporting: recent constipation; opposing: bowels now normal, pain localized, no GI upset currently.

Issue 1 – Suspected UTI / Lower abdominal pain:
• Empiric antibiotic: Trimethoprim 1 tab BID × 3 days (script sent to pharmacy).  
• Symptomatic care: Adequate oral hydration, cranberry juice, paracetamol for pain.  
• Safety net: Return urgently if pain worsens, fever develops, vomiting, flank pain, or no improvement in 48–72 h.  
• Follow-up: Review in a few days or sooner if concerns.

Issue 2 – Rule out pregnancy:
• Home urine pregnancy test advised today.  
• If positive or pain worsens, seek immediate medical review to exclude ectopic pregnancy.

Issue 3 – Diagnostic clarification:
• If no improvement/negative pregnancy test: obtain urinalysis ± culture, full blood count, renal function, and consider pelvic ultrasound.  
• Consider GI or gynecologic referral depending on course.

General plan items:
• Provide written information on UTI symptoms/red flags.  
• Ensure easy access for telehealth or in-person follow-up.

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: Allergies, vitals, physical examination findings, medication doses for Implanon and paracetamol.  
● No contradictions noted between transcript and reasoning.  
● Transcript quality: Clear conversation; no significant inaudible sections.
